title: Check-In Rules for Paying a Visit from a Self-Pay Visit Package
content:
Visits are drawn only from a Self-Pay Visit Package in **active** status; the status shown on that package's own record is what decides it. A standard 45-minute, aquatic or post-operative visit draws one package visit; an extended 60-minute or specialty one-on-one visit draws the tier's extended-visit draw. Telehealth visits are paid from the package only where the tier makes telehealth payable, aquatic visits only where it makes aquatic therapy payable, and specialty visits only where it makes specialty visits payable; a visit the package cannot pay is charged the single-visit cash rate. When the last visit is drawn the package is exhausted.

**Input, judgement, output**

| Visit format attended | Payable from the package when | Package visits drawn |
|---|---|---|
| Standard 45-minute | always, on an active package | 1 |
| Post-operative | always, on an active package | 1 |
| Aquatic | the tier makes aquatic visits payable | 1 |
| Telehealth | the tier makes telehealth visits payable | 1 |
| Extended 60-minute | always, on an active package | the tier's extended-visit draw |
| Specialty one-on-one | the tier makes specialty visits payable | the tier's extended-visit draw |

**Points of judgement**

- *Package status other than active* (pending payment, frozen, exhausted, expired or cancelled): no visit is drawn from it.
- *A format the tier does not make payable:* the visit is charged the single-visit cash rate instead of being drawn from the package.
- *The visit that uses the last remaining package visit:* the package becomes exhausted.

*Hypothetical case:* an active package with 3 visits remaining, on a tier whose extended-visit draw is 2, pays an extended 60-minute visit by drawing 2 visits and is left with 1.
